synthesis.verdict: Structurally the codebase is on solid footing: the app→server-page→client-component→lib pattern is real and mostly honored, most lib modules ship unit tests, the strict-TS config is genuinely strong, and the core designs (error-handler funnel, lib/clipboard, the Zustand storage concurrency-lock, the off-thread regex/ReDoS worker, Next.js route error boundaries) are well-built. The dominant drag on maintainability is accumulated dead weight — roughly 5,000+ LOC of unreferenced UI primitives, an orphaned animation showcase and its transitive dependents, an abandoned Zustand-migration subtree, dead CSS, and 19 orphaned npm deps — compounded by systemic copy-paste of browser-IO helpers (blob-download, FileReader-to-Promise, clipboard, formatBytes) that no shared util captures. Good utilities exist but are under-adopted, and the total absence of a formatter/lint baseline lets style and convention drift rot unchecked. The correct posture is consolidation and enforcement, not redesign: delete the dead code, add tooling, extract the shared helpers, then adopt the funnels that already exist.
strengths: The app→server-page→client-component→lib architecture is real and largely followed, and the pure-logic lib modules (calculator, hash, base64, json, regex-tester, markdown, snippet-generator) already ship unit tests — keep both the pattern and these existing suites; the fix is to pull the few stragglers (SQL, image, calculator scientific math) into it, not to change the pattern.

The strict TypeScript config (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitReturns, etc.) is a genuine asset — do not relax it; the `any`/`as never` findings are the code failing to live up to the config, not the config being wrong.

The error-handling design (getUserFriendlyError + logError + sanitizeErrorMessage) is well-built and is the right funnel — do not rewrite it; the remediation is to adopt/wire it (e.g. LC-05 wires the orphaned sanitizer in), not replace it.
lib/clipboard.ts copyToClipboard (secure-context guard + DOMException handling) is solid and already used by ~8 components — standardize the raw-writeText stragglers onto it rather than reinventing.

The Next.js route error boundaries (app/error.tsx, app/global-error.tsx) are correctly wired and are the right approach — the standalone components/error-boundary.tsx is merely redundant, not a gap to fill.

The live Zustand storage path (tool-settings + storage.ts per-key promise-chain concurrency lock + types.ts) is sophisticated and correct — preserve it; only the abandoned migration/provider/orphan-store subtree wrapped around it is dead.

Live visual/animation infrastructure — pixel-blast + LandingBackground, PageTransition, and the 7 actually-used animation variants — is functioning and must be preserved through the dead-code sweep (the audit already flagged pixel-blast, page-transition, sonner-pkg, three/postprocessing as deletion false-positives to exclude).

themes.name: Repo-wide dead-weight
themes.summary: The single largest issue: ~5,000+ LOC that never runs — 26 zero-importer shadcn UI files (~2,663 LOC) and their 19 orphaned npm deps, a 348-LOC animations-showcase demo dragging 7 more custom UI files (~1,067 LOC) into transitive death, an abandoned Zustand-migration subtree (provider/barrel/migration/two orphan stores, ~571 LOC), ~180 LOC of dead CSS, a dead sonner wrapper, dead error/storage helpers, five orphaned tool sub-components, dead controls (password 'Full words' no-op), stale developer-monologue comments, and numerous dead exports/constants/state. Several findings (XX-*, CU-03/CS-01) are the same deletions surfaced by different audit passes and should be de-duplicated during execution.
themes.leverage: Highest leverage by far — pure behavior-preserving deletion with near-zero runtime risk that removes the bulk of the maintenance surface, shrinks the bundle, eliminates several `any`-holes for free, and unblocks/simplifies every later refactor (barrels stop needing lockstep edits, dep prune becomes possible). 9 of the 12 P0s live here.

themes.name: Cross-page presentational duplication & factories
themes.summary: The same UI scaffolding is hand-copied across many pages/components: the 'Last updated' block in 13 tool pages, near-identical Metadata objects across 24 pages (banner literal in 19), the animated page-header across explore/tools/games and again across the game clients, the game-over overlay across dino/snake, convert-view vs generate-view (~80% clones), the CommandDialog results list in two nav components, the GitHub contributors fetch+type in footer and contribute-client, and the debounced-fetch+From/To layout across the two currency converters and unit-converter. Plus small consistency items (local fadeInUp copies, ⌘K hardcoded vs platform-detected, EXCLUDED_USERS in-body, content-grid re-alias).
themes.leverage: Medium-high: a handful of shared components/helpers (LastUpdated, createToolMetadata, PageHeader/GameHeader, GameOverOverlay, OutputPanel, CommandResults, useContributors, useIsMac) each retire many duplicated call sites and make future tools/games consistent by construction.

themes.name: Browser-IO & formatting utility duplication
themes.summary: One fundamental operation reimplemented everywhere with no shared home (lib/utils.ts only exports cn): the createObjectURL→anchor→click→revoke blob-download dance appears in 9 places (with correctness drift between sync and deferred revoke), the FileReader-to-Promise wrapper in 6, formatBytes in 4 named copies plus 4 inline sites, the copy-then-toast block in ~11 sites, and byte-limit constants collide/re-derive (MAX_FILE_BYTES means 25MB in one module and 5MB in another). The API-layer fetch/ok-check/json boilerplate is a smaller sibling.
themes.leverage: High: extracting lib/download.ts, lib/file-reader.ts, lib/format.ts (formatBytes + byte consts) and a hooks/use-copy-to-clipboard.ts collapses hundreds of duplicated LOC into single sources of truth, fixes the download-revoke divergence uniformly, and gives later component surgery a clean utility layer to lean on. 2 P0s here.

themes.name: God components & logic trapped in the UI layer
themes.summary: Pure, testable logic lives inside client components instead of lib/: the entire SQL beautify algorithm, calculator DEG/RAD+epsilon-snapping trig, the 80-line Base64 derive-effect, and canvas resize/estimate math all sit in components with no lib module or tests. Separately, several components are oversized single functions — RegexTesterClient (335 LOC, ~14 concerns), buildExplainTree (275-line 20-arm switch), pixel-blast (728 LOC), dino-client (147 LOC two-mode), contribute-client (313 LOC), plus the calculator keypad's ~195 lines of repetitive JSX and drawCard's ~100 lines of unnamed layout literals.
themes.leverage: High structural win: extracting the pure transforms into lib/[tool]/* makes user-facing behavior unit-testable for the first time (SQL, calculator trig, base64 derive, image estimate are all currently uncovered), and decomposing the god-components makes them safely editable. Extraction is behavior-preserving and low-risk; the deep decomposition is where care is needed.

themes.name: Tooling, config & style-enforcement gaps
themes.summary: The documented style (double quotes, semicolons, 2-space indent, trailing commas, ≤100 col) has zero enforcement — no Prettier config/dependency, no format script, and eslint.config.mjs only extends next+core-web-vitals (which it also redundantly double-loads). Consequently multiple clusters drifted: legacy lib files, all of lib/games, image/currency/units/music, ~44/60 ui files, and middleware/stats route use single quotes and/or omit semicolons. Also: package.json name is the scaffold 'nextjs', the CoinGecko API key is hardcoded/committed, and Button's size variants sit below the documented 44px touch-target minimum.
themes.leverage: Medium and a force-multiplier: adding a Prettier config + format script (and de-duping the eslint config) lets a single mechanical pass fix all the style-drift findings at once and prevents recurrence, which is exactly how the drift accumulated. Best run once, after the dead files are deleted so the formatter never touches them.

themes.name: Games cluster consolidation & gameplay completion
themes.summary: The games modules are a coherent outlier: no shared game-loop hook (setInterval-in-useEffect + keydown plumbing hand-rolled per game), Snake tears down/recreates its interval every tick and direction change, magic numbers scattered instead of in GAME_CONFIG, and duplicated initial-state literals. Convention-wise, no game client respects useReducedMotion, none use cn() for conditional classes, and every lib/games file breaks the quote/semicolon style. Two gameplay bugs make custom Dino non-functional (collision treats obstacle.height as a y-coordinate so jumps never clear, and no code path ever calls startGame from idle) — both WIP-gated so blast radius is contained.

The gameplay fixes are behavior-changing and should ship only when the WIP feature is intentionally finished.

themes.name: User-visible correctness defects
themes.summary: Real bugs shipped to (or reachable by) users: the Scientific Calculator returns NaN for any parenthesized or percent input like '2*(3+4)' or '50%' (a v2 regression) and treats ^ as left-associative; the Area unit dropdown shows 'Icon (ac)' instead of 'Acre'; the SQL formatter's replace-order makes LEFT/RIGHT/INNER JOIN handling dead and mangles word-internal OR/AND; markdown/regex page titles render a double '| astraa | Astraa' suffix; the Memory game shows 4-of-a-kind faces (6 unique emojis for 8 pairs). Optional/robustness: hash tool imports Node crypto in a client component.
themes.leverage: Highest user-facing priority even though several are behavior-changing rather than pure refactors — the calculator NaN is a P0 correctness regression on a core tool. These need characterization tests locking the corrected behavior and should not be blocked behind the structural work.

themes.name: Error-handling & clipboard convention drift
themes.summary: Well-designed funnels exist but are bypassed. The external API layer and both currency converters use raw console.*/inline toast strings instead of getUserFriendlyError()+logError(); crypto-converter swallows failures silently (no toast) and drops `toast` from its effect deps; four JSON copy paths call navigator.clipboard.writeText with no try/catch (unhandled rejection + false 'Copied' toast) instead of copyToClipboard; and sanitizeErrorMessage sits orphaned so the documented path/URL/email/IP redaction never actually runs.
themes.leverage: Medium-high: routing every error/clipboard path through the existing helpers makes failure behavior consistent and observable, fulfills a documented (currently-unmet) sanitization guarantee, and eliminates unhandled promise rejections — all by adopting infra that already exists rather than building anything new.

themes.name: Type-safety erosion
themes.summary: `any` and unsafe casts undercut the strict config in the exact spots that most need typing: untyped response.json() in the API layer, `any` in store types and every zustand migrate() signature, three `as never` casts laundering Shiki's literal unions, a missing explicit return type on the generateText server action plus non-null env assertions in redis, and stringly-typed 'Temperature' dispatch coupling data labels to conversion logic.
themes.leverage: Medium: type-only, mostly behavior-preserving changes that restore compile-time protection on external-payload and persisted-data boundaries; note that some `any`-holes (dead hooks LA-03, dead password-options CA-06) are already erased by the dead-code sweep, so scope this to the live surface after Theme A.

themes.name: Store/storage layer & latent async robustness
themes.summary: Beyond the dead migration subtree, the live storage layer has correctness/robustness latents: ParseClient.destroy() clears pending promises without resolving them (awaiters hang, closures over up-to-50MB text stranded); IndexedDBAdapter opens a fresh un-closed DB connection on every read/write; the SSR-fallback LocalStorageAdapter touches localStorage with no window guard in the exact branch it's selected for; recursive JsonValue walkers (sortDeep/tsType/zodOf/json-schema) have no depth cap on 50MB inputs; and the concurrency-lock/enqueue logic has no unit tests while sibling stores do.
themes.leverage: Medium: cheap hardening (memoize the DB handle, guard the fallback, resolve pending on destroy) plus a depth cap and a storage.test.ts that pins the subtle enqueue lock — protects the one piece of infra whose whole reason for existing is preventing races, with mostly behavior-preserving changes.

findings.title: Snake game loop tears down and recreates its interval on every state change

Then the interval keys only on GAME_SPEED and never resets on direction/tick changes. This alters tick-timing under rapid input, so mark it non-behavior-preserving; add/adjust a characterization test for the eat-food grow path.

findings.title: Anchor-click blob download reimplemented in 9 places
findings.locations: lib/snippet-generator/export.ts:32-41 (exported downloadBlob(blob,name)); lib/markdown/export.ts:1-8 (private downloadBlob(blob,name)); lib/base64/download.ts:1-18 (downloadAsFile(content,name,mime)); components/regex-tester/matches-panel.tsx:28-38 (private downloadBlob(content,name,mime)); components/json/toolbar.tsx:53-63 (inline onDownload); components/json/generate-view.tsx:70-80 (inline); components/json/convert-view.tsx:79-89 (inline); components/regex-tester/snippet-card-export.tsx:206-213 (inline); lib/image/image-utils.ts:47-56 (inline in canvas.toBlob cb)
findings.smell: The exact createObjectURL -> createElement('a') -> set href/download -> click -> revoke sequence is hand-written 9 times. Two shapes recur: takes a Blob (snippet, markdown, snippet-card, image), or takes content+mime and builds the Blob (base64 downloadAsFile, matches-panel downloadBlob, and 3 identical JSON onDownload handlers). No shared download util exists (lib/utils.ts only exports cn). Sites also diverge in correctness: markdown/export.ts:7 and image-utils.ts:55 revoke the object URL synchronously right after .click() (can abort the download in some browsers) while the other 7 defer via setTimeout(...,0); only some append the anchor to document.body.
findings.change: Create lib/download.ts exporting downloadBlob(blob: Blob, filename: string): void using the robust variant (append anchor to body, click, removeChild, window.setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 0)) and downloadContent(content: string | Uint8Array, filename: string, mime: string): void that builds the Blob then calls downloadBlob. Replace all 9 sites: lib/snippet-generator/export.ts and lib/markdown/export.ts import (and can re-export) downloadBlob; delete the private copies in lib/markdown/export.ts:1-8 and components/regex-tester/matches-panel.tsx:28-38; lib/base64/download.ts becomes a thin re-export of downloadContent (or callers import directly); the 3 JSON onDownload handlers and snippet-card-export call downloadContent/downloadBlob; image-utils.ts:47-56 calls downloadBlob inside its toBlob callback. No unit tests cover these paths, so no test churn; the synchronous->deferred revoke change is strictly safer and preserves the download.
findings.note: All 9 sites verified at exact cited lines; lib/utils.ts exports only cn; sync-revoke at markdown/export.ts:7 and image-utils.ts:55 vs deferred setTimeout elsewhere confirmed; no lib/download.ts exists.
